Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Intertwined ferromagnetic and altermagnetic orders in Cr-doped MnTe
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Jonathan M. DeStefano, Yaofeng Xie, Guodong Ren, Mai Nguyen, Yue Sun, Xiaodong Xu, Juan Carlos Idrobo, Jiun-Haw Chu
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Ferromagnetism and altermagnetism both break time-reversal symmetry, yet their distinct transformation properties under crystalline symmetries forbid direct bilinear coupling between their order parameters. Whether these two magnetic orders can remain thermodynamically distinct while strongly influencing one another remains an open question. Here we demonstrate the homogeneous coexistence of ferromagnetism and altermagnetism in Cr-doped MnTe. By tuning the ferromagnetic ordering temperature across the nearly unchanged Néel temperature with Cr doping, we uncover a striking interplay between the two orders: the ferromagnetic transition becomes a crossover when altermagnetism develops first, whereas the onset of altermagnetism strongly suppresses the out-of-plane ferromagnetic remanence when ferromagnetism develops first. Moreover, spin-orbit coupling enables symmetry-selective interactions through which the ferromagnetic moment controls the altermagnetic domain manifold, with its out-of-plane and in-plane components biasing the time-reversal ($Z_2$) and orientational ($Z_3$) sectors, respectively. Our results reveal how two symmetry-distinct magnetic orders can retain separate ordering tendencies while remaining strongly coupled, providing a route towards internal control of altermagnetic domain states.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Control of the Electronic and Atomic Structure of the Altermagnetic α-MnTe Surface via Substrate-Induced Surfactants
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Martin Heinrich, Mahdi Hajlaoui, Takuya Takashiro, Tetiana Zakusylo, Petr Babor, Ondrej Caha, Dawid Wutke, Natalia Olszowska, Gunther Springholz, Matthias Muntwiler
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnets are a novel class of materials with unique momentum dependent spin-polarization of the electronic band structure, which opens up new avenues for spintronic devices. Altermagnetic α-MnTe is particularly interesting for such applications due to its giant spin splitting and the persistence of altermagnetic order up to room temperature. Growth of thin films is, however, challenging and governed by interactions with the substrate. As a result, the surface of α-MnTe thin films exhibits very different atomic structures in dependence of the substrate material. Whereas on SrF2(111) an atomically clean, perfectly (2x2) reconstructed surface forms, on InP(111)A the MnTe surface is always InTe terminated due to super-segregation of In from the substrate to the surface. Most strikingly, the InTe surfactant layer displays a quasi-periodic dislocation network to accommodate the InTe/MnTe lattice mismatch. This leads to the emergence of distinct surface states in dependence of surface termination that strongly affect the electronic band structure at the surface as shown by angle resolved photoemission and tunneling spectroscopy. Thus, control and characterization of the atomic structure of the surface is fundamentally important for understanding the properties of altermagnets and provides room for engineering and tailoring of spin-polarized states in actual devices.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Spontaneous Circular Dichroism and Memory Effect from Surface Defects in Altermagnetic MnTe
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Benjamin F. Mead, Isaiah Gray, Seng Huat Lee, Michael Chilcote, Zi-Jie Yan, Sijie Xu, Aparna Jayakumar, Emilia Morosan, Jörn W. F. Venderbos, Cui-Zu Chang, Zhiqiang Mao, Pengcheng Dai, Matthew Brahlek, Liang Wu
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnetism has emerged as a new class of magnetism with vanishing magnetization and macroscopic time reversal symmetry breaking. Hexagonal MnTe is a g-wave altermagnet with a 307 K Néel temperature, large spin splitting, and an anomalous Hall effect. However, the relationship between altermagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect in MnTe remains debated. Here, using optical magnetic circular dichroism, we observe hysteresis and a memory effect in a MnTe bulk crystal below 250 K. No hysteresis is seen after polishing the bulk crystal and in thin films. We conclude that the hysteresis in magnetic circular dichroism in the bulk crystal is from surface defects. The similar temperature dependence and a sign change between circular dichroism and the anomalous Hall effect indicate that the origin of the anomalous Hall effect in transport is likely not intrinsic.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Anisotropic spin splitting in $α$-MnTe epilayers on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Zofia Kopacz-Maj, Ali Akbar, Aleksandr Kazakov, Bartłomiej Turowski, Wojciech Zaleszczyk, Marta Aleszkiewicz, Tomasz Wojciechowski, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Natalia Olszowska, Tomasz Wojtowicz, Valentine V. Volobuev
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: $α$-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial $α$-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the $Γ$-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along $Γ$-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for $α$-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Weiwei Chen, Ziyu Zhou, Pan Gao, Yanan Pan, Zhongjun Li, Ye Yang, Jianhui Zhou, Rui Wang
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $Γ$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane Néel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the Néel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the Néel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing Néel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Berry curvature quadrupole induced third-order anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Jiacheng Yao, Zhuocheng Lu, Zhichao Guo, Hua Wang
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, providing a symmetry-rich platform for exploring nonlinear quantum-geometric transport. In the d-wave altermagnet considered here, the antiunitary symmetry operation $TC_{4z}$ enforces a vanishing momentum-integrated Berry curvature, while inversion symmetry forbids a finite Berry-curvature dipole. Consequently, the Berry curvature quadrupole (BCQ) can provide a contribution to the nonlinear Hall response, scaling as $τ^2$, where $τ$ denotes the relaxation time. We derive a gauge-covariant Wannier interpolation formula that enables efficient evaluation of the BCQ directly from first-principles Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians. Applying this framework to $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$, we calculate the momentum-space distribution of the BCQ and the associated chemical potential dependent nonlinear conductivity. The momentum-resolved analysis reveals that the dominant contribution originates from spin-orbit coupling induced avoided arossings, directly linking the gap structure to the sign-changing nonlinear response. Our work establishes a general first-principles route to higher-order quantum-geometric responses in altermagnets, opening avenues for exploring nonlinear Hall effects in next-generation spintronic and magnetoelectronic devices.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Uniaxial strain-induced multipiezo effect in two-dimensional multifunctional altermagnet Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Bocheng Lei, Aolin Li, Wenzhe Zhou, Bei Zhang, Yunpeng Wang, Fangping Ouyang
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnetism has attracted considerable attention in recent years. As an emerging magnetic phase, it features collinear antiferromagnetic order, yielding a zero net magnetic moment and nonrelativistic spin splitting. Using density functional theory, we reported five stable semiconducting altermagnetic monolayers: Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO (X, Y = S, Se, Te, X ≠ Y). These monolayers exhibit C-paired spin–valley locking, strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy, a strain-tunable piezovalley response, and strain-induced magnetization assisted by carrier doping. Distinct from previously reported two-dimensional altermagnets, these five materials exhibit pronounced valley polarization under uniaxial strain, which primarily originates from the p orbitals of the chalcogen atoms. The out-of-plane piezoelectricity of Janus Cr2XYO monolayers arises from the electronegativity difference between the X and Y atoms. Among them, Cr2Te2O exhibits the largest valley polarization of 222 meV under −4% uniaxial strain, while Cr2STeO exhibits a sizable out-of-plane piezoelectric response with a d31 coefficient of 0.63 pm/V. Our results reveal a multipiezo effect in Cr2X2O and Janus Cr2XYO monolayers that integrates spin, valley, and mechanical degrees of freedom, thereby establishing a multifunctional material system for valleytronics, spintronics, and flexible piezoelectric devices.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Mirror-symmetry engineering of altermagnetism based on monolayer hexagonal lattices
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Han-Bing Li, Zhi-Gang Shao
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. The N$-$H structure forms a stable altermagnetic ground state, with a momentum-dependent spin splitting up to 148.2 meV. The magnetism originates from $π-π$ superexchange interactions, and H/F functionalization stabilizes intrinsic AM by regulating the local charge distribution. Our work offers insights into the design of light-element altermagnetic materials.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Koki Mizuno
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed Néel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the Néel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Light-induced chiral altermagnets from conventional antiferromagnets
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Jorge Cardenas-Gamboa, Devika Jayadeep, Aritz Leonardo, Gregory A. Fiete, Jeroen van den Brink, Maia G. Vergniory
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated collinear magnetic order with momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering new opportunities for spintronic applications. Here, we propose a route to optically induce altermagnetism through coherent lattice control. Using symmetry analysis, we identify phonon distortions that lift the spin degeneracy of conventional antiferromagnets while preserving the rotational symmetries connecting opposite-spin sublattices. Among these, geometric chiral phonons provide a particularly appealing pathway, linking the emergence of altermagnetism to structural chirality. Taking Fe$_2$TeO$_6$ as a prototype, we demonstrate that a linearly polarized mid-infrared pulse can drive a structural instability through negative biquadratic coupling between an infrared-active phonon and an optically silent, symmetry-breaking mode. First-principles-based lattice dynamics reveal the emergence of a transient chiral distortion, while electronic-structure calculations establish that the light-induced structure exhibits nonrelativistic spin splitting characteristic of altermagnetism. Our results establish a symmetry-guided pathway toward the ultrafast optical control of altermagnetic states through nonlinear phononics.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Sundeep Kapila, Bhaskaran Muralidharan, Satadeep Bhattacharjee
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbital contributions and guide systematic basis set refinement and optimizes parameters through weights. The resulting Hamiltonian can be used to evaluate anomalous (AHC) and spin Hall conductivities (SHC), and topological invariants. We demonstrate the framework using eight representative materials spanning semimetals, semiconductors, transition metals, f-electron compounds, and magnetic systems. Symmetry resolved models achieve band energy errors of 9 to 41 meV within 1 eV of the Fermi level. The fitted Hamiltonians reproduce characteristic features of the SHC response of Pt, the SOC dependence of the AHC of Fe, and the momentum dependent altermagnetic spin splitting of MnTe without any altermagnet specific interaction. For EuMn2Bi2, projection guided orbital refinement reduces the near Fermi level fitting error from 120 to 32 meV. Together, these results establish SKFitter as a flexible and reproducible framework for developing symmetry consistent, physically interpretable TB models of complex materials.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Two-Dimensional Magnetic Materials from Ferromagnetism to Altermagnetism: Fabrication, Symmetry, Evidence, and Device Readiness
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Guojian Zhao, Ziang Meng, Li Liu, Zhiyuan Duan, Jingyu Li, Sixu Jiang, Xiaoyang Tan, Shiheng Bu, Chen Liang, Xiaoning Wang, Peixin Qin, Zhiqi Liu
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Atomically thin magnets are governed by composition, thickness, stacking, strain, defects, substrates, ferroic order, and interfaces. This Review organizes two-dimensional (2D) magnetism using net magnetization and momentum-space spin splitting or spin-polarization patterns as primary coordinates, supplemented by sublattice structure and the symmetry relations between opposite-spin sublattices. Ferromagnets generally carry a net moment; ferrimagnets can be fully compensated. Conventional antiferromagnets may retain spin-degenerate bands, while altermagnets permit nonrelativistic alternating spin splitting under dimension-specific symmetry constraints. M1-M4 reporting classes introduced here distinguish layer-resolved atomically thin forms, non-layer-resolved thin flakes or films, bulk benchmarks, and theoretical candidates or design routes; the evidence category and ordering-temperature provenance are reported independently. Current experimental support for altermagnetism comes mainly from M2 thin-film and M3 bulk benchmarks, leaving a fully verified atomically thin M1 altermagnetic phase as an open experimental goal. Most proposed monolayer and few-layer systems therefore fall within M4, and contested cases clarify the measurements needed for phase assignment. Device readiness is compared qualitatively using operating temperature, readout, switching, domain control, stability, scalability, interface sensitivity, and integration difficulty. Reliable phase assignment and device assessment require complementary measurements from the same material form under matched conditions, ideally on the same specimen or in situ.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Meta-Altermagnetism and Enhanced Spin-Splitting
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Bogeng Wen, Hae-Young Kee
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnets with zero net magnetization and spin-split electronic bands. Here, we explore whether altermagnetism can exhibit a discontinuous jump, a phenomenon we refer to as meta-altermagnetism. We show that meta-altermagnetism can emerge in 2D systems when magnetic-order-induced band reconstruction drives spin-split van Hove singularities (vHSs) across the Fermi level. Using mean-field theory for an extended $t$-$J$ model on a two-sublattice square lattice including anisotropic hopping integral, we find that a first-order meta-altermagnetic transition produces an intermediate altermagnetic regime with reduced staggered magnetization but strongly enhanced magnetic octupole and time-reversal-odd spin-splitter conductivity. We further show that the first-order transition line terminates at a quantum critical endpoint, giving rise to a rich phase diagram as the chemical potential and anisotropic hopping strength are varied. Our results identify the spin split vHSs as a route to enhancing spin-splitter effect for spintronic applications.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Flexural Altermagnetism
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Songbo Li, Jinxiong Jia, Zeyu Li, Xudong Zhu, Jiaqi An, Feitong Chu, Songbo Zhang, Wenguang Zhu, Hualing Zeng, Zhenhua Qiao
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: We establish flexural deformation as a versatile route for engineering altermagnetism in two-dimensional collinear antiferromagnets. By tailoring the flexure, we selectively break different symmetries to realize altermagnetic states with distinct wave symmetries and reverse their spin splitting. A tight-binding model and first-principles calculations for monolayer MnPS3 demonstrate d- and i-wave states and a switchable transverse spin current in the d-wave state.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Modulated exchange bias and antisymmetric magnetoresistance at a spin–flop coupled van der Waals interface of FeTe/Fe3GeTe2
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Wei Jiang, Qian Chen, Xingze Dai, Liang He, Wen Zhang, Zhaocong Huang, Ya Zhai
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: We construct a van der Waals heterostructure of FeTe/Fe3GeTe2 (FGT), which presents a spin-orthogonal interface and exchange bias effect. The underlying mechanism of the observed bias field is ascribed to proximity-induced uncompensated interfacial moments in FeTe, which act as effective pinning centers for the magnetization reversal in Fe3GeTe2 and whose configuration is set by the field-cooling and subsequent field-sweep history. Field-sweep history plays an important role in this effect: in asymmetric field-sweep protocols, the bias field shows a clear and systematic trend with the reversing field and can be continuously tuned from −300 to +200 Oe. Interestingly, the effect persists up to about 100 K, well above the Néel temperature of bulk FeTe (∼65 K). These are accompanied by antisymmetric magnetoresistance, arising from the asynchronous reversal of the FGT surface and bulk layers together with interfacial spin-dependent scattering. We attribute the above findings to a spin–flop coupling arising from the FeTe/Fe3GeTe2 interface and the reconfigurable interfacial pinning moments under asymmetric field-sweep protocols. This work provides a new route toward van der Waals spintronic devices based on the reconfigurable exchange bias effect and multi-resistance state functionality.

Watched authors.title: Electric Field-Induced Hole- and Electron-Type Flat Bands in Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene
Watched authors.authors: Zhihao Jiang, Dongkyu Lee, Alfred J. H. Jones, Youngju Park, Paulina Majchrzak, Kimberly Hsieh, Chakradhar Sahoo, Thomas S. Nielsen, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Philip Hofmann, Yong P. Chen, Jeil Jung, Søren Ulstrup
Watched authors.abstract: Application of a finite electric field and small twist angle between two graphene bilayers leads to widely tunable electronic structures that support emergent phenomena. Here, we measure the electronic structure of twisted double bilayer graphene with twist angles of 3.1$^{\circ}$ and 6.0$^{\circ}$ using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (microARPES) on \textit{in situ} gated samples. At a twist angle of 6.0$^{\circ}$, we find that the dispersion around the valence and conduction band extrema is unchanged compared to separate graphene bilayers, whereas electric field tunable hybridisation gaps and band flattening effects occur at higher binding energies. In the 3.1$^{\circ}$ structure, we find that the resulting superlattice drives dispersion changes around the valence and conduction band edges. Increasing the gate-induced doping in the bottom bilayer leads to the formation of flat bands between the valence band maximum in the bottom bilayer and conduction band minimum in the top bilayer. Our experiments establish combinations of twist angle and electric field that potentially support strong electron-hole excitations and that provide a benchmark for the theoretical description of moderately twisted double bilayer graphene.
